examples.text: Donner des démentis est à la portée du premier imbécile venu. C'est une forme de l’idémisme, de l'automatisme mental. Mais réfuter une objection ! Voilà qui n'est pas votre fait.

glosses: Choses qui se trouvent contraires à une assertion, à une conjecture, etc.

examples.text: Ces faits donnent un démenti formel à votre assertion, à ceux qui prétendent que…

glosses: Désagrément qu’on éprouve en échouant dans une entreprise, dans une tentative dont on avait le succès à cœur.

examples.text: Il a entrepris cela, et je crois qu’il en aura le démenti.
Je n’en aurai pas, je ne veux pas en avoir le démenti.

Il s’aperçoit alors qu’on l’a trompé de nouveau. Cependant il ne veut point en avoir le démenti ; et, comme si son honneur eût été intéressé à cette aventure, il jure de n’en sortir, d’une manière ou de l’autre, que victorieux.

translations.source_sense_description: Action de nier la véracité de ce que quelqu’un a a affirmé.

glosses: An assertion of untruth.

examples.text: The singer has issued a sweeping denial of all the rumors.

glosses: The negation in logic.

examples.text: The denial of "There might be X" is the null, "False, there is no X."

glosses: A refusal or failure to provide or grant something that is requested or desired.

examples.text: The denial of medical treatment to those who cannot afford to pay is scandalous.
I cannot understand the bank's denial of my loan application.
Every time we asked for an interview we got a denial.

glosses: Refusal to believe that a problem exists.

examples.text: We couldn't break through his denial about being alcoholic.

Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic […]. Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become. When a series of bank failures made this impossible, there was widespread anger, leading to the public humiliation of symbolic figures.

glosses: Refusal to admit responsibility for wrongdoing.

examples.text: Denial is the first act when the perpetrator refutes the very nature of the planned measures, explaining the steps as justified and legitimate actions to cope with the identified problem. The denial then lives on during the different stages of the genocide and is invoked continuously by the perpetrator whenever its actions are criticized or labeled as atrocities and unlawful. At the end, once the practical stages have had their course, all that remains and thrives is the denial.

glosses: Negationism, denialism of historical facts or accepted interpretation.

examples.text: However, just as genocide is understood by some—including Raphael Lemkin—as a kind of radical, perverse act of creation, so too, denial does not aim only at a negation of reality but also at the creation of a new reality.

The sheer length of the list demonstrates the hold denial wields over states and societies, a power that may be best understood empirically by delving further into the two best-documented cases of Holocaust and Armenian [genocide] denial.

glosses: A defense mechanism involving a refusal to accept the truth of a phenomenon or prospect.

examples.text: He is in denial that he has a drinking problem.

"Denial" came out of the therapyspeak prevalent in the middle of the 20th century, especially as it was applied to confronting the reality of mortality. It was popularized as the first stage of grief, and quickly expanded to include refusal to confront any bad news or disturbing ideas.

glosses: A disownment or disavowal

examples.text: The denial of Jesus by Peter.

glosses: To rest in a horizontal position on a surface.

examples.text: The book lies on the table; the snow lies on the roof; he lies in his coffin.
Under an oak were lying asleep a pair of shepherds.
Though ye haue lien among the pots, yet shall yee bee as the wings of a doue, couered with siluer, and her feathers with yellow gold.

glosses: To be placed or situated.

examples.text: Ying-yang county lies 70 li southwest of the modern Teng-feng county, Honan.

glosses: To abide; to remain for a longer or shorter time; to be in a certain state or condition.

examples.text: to lie waste; to lie fallow; to lie open; to lie hidden; to lie grieving; to lie under one's displeasure; to lie at the mercy of the waves

glosses: Used with in: to be or exist; to belong or pertain; to have an abiding place; to consist.

examples.text: Envy lies between beings equal in nature, though unequal in circumstances.

glosses: Used with with: to have sexual relations with.

examples.text: And it came to passe after these things, that his masters wife cast her eyes vpon Ioseph, and shee said, Lie with me.

glosses: Used with on/upon: to be incumbent (on); to be the responsibility of a person.

examples.text: While I was now trifling at home, I saw London, […] where I lay one night only.

glosses: To be still or quiet, like one lying down to rest.

examples.text: The Wind is lowd, and will not lie till the Ship be cleard of the dead.

glosses: To be sustainable; to be capable of being maintained.

examples.text: An appeal lies in this case from the ordinary to the arches.

glosses: The terrain and conditions surrounding the ball before it is struck.

examples.text: When Pinocchio lies, his nose grows.

glosses: To convey a false image or impression.

examples.text: Photographs often lie.

glosses: To be mistaken or unintentionally spread false information.

examples.text: Sorry, I haven't seen your keys anywhere...wait, I lied! They're right there on the coffee table.

glosses: An intentionally false statement; an intentional falsehood.

examples.text: I knew he was telling a lie by his facial expression.
Man everywhere is the born enemy of lies.

glosses: A statement intended to deceive, even if literally true.
Anything that misleads or disappoints.

examples.text: Wishing this lie of life was o'er.

glosses: A liar; a dishonest person.
